overview: The Song dynasty oversaw an economic and technological revolution in China, though military weakness led to the loss of northern China in 1127. Printing, gunpowder, the compass and paper money transformed society, while Neo-Confucianism shaped intellectual life.

items.text: Bi Sheng invents movable type printing, though woodblock remained more common.
Shen Kuo describes the magnetic compass for navigation in his Dream Pool Essays.
The first gunpowder formula for military use appears in the Wujing Zongyao military manual.
Paper money issued by the government to facilitate commerce.
Improved agricultural techniques with early-ripening rice varieties from Vietnam.
Landscape painting reaches its peak with masters like Fan Kuan and Guo Xi.
Porcelain production perfects celadon and qingbai wares.
Zhu Xi synthesizes Neo-Confucianism, combining Confucian ethics with metaphysical speculation.
Maritime trade with Southeast Asia, India and the Middle East expands dramatically.
Porcelain exported throughout Asia and eventually to the Middle East and Africa.
Song technological innovations transformed the world when transmitted to Europe.
Neo-Confucianism became the dominant ideology in East Asia until the nineteenth century.

fall.text: The Mongol conquest completed when the last Song emperor drowned during the fall of the final Song stronghold in 1279.
